es.summary: Disminución de la capacidad de la placenta para transferir oxígeno y nutrientes al feto, provocando restricción del crecimiento y posible oligohidramnios. Se diagnostica mediante ecografía y medición del índice de líquido amniótico.
key_points: Se asocia a crecimiento fetal restringido y bajo volumen de líquido amniótico
Diagnóstico por ecografía: AFI <5 cm o saco amniótico <500 mL
Manejo incluye reposo, hidratación materna y monitorización fetal
Complicaciones: parto prematuro, sufrimiento fetal y muerte intrauterina

pathophysiology: Placenta no logra perfusión adecuada por insuficiente remodelación vascular
Disminuye el intercambio de oxígeno y nutrientes entre madre y feto
Resultado: hipoxia fetal y reducción del volumen de líquido amniótico
signs_symptoms: Crecimiento uterino menor al esperado para la edad gestacional
diagnostics: Ecografía obstétrica: AFI <5 cm o saco amniótico <500 mL
Doppler de arteria umbilical: flujo anormal o aumento de la resistencia
Biometría fetal: percentil <10 para edad gestacional
Pruebas de bienestar fetal: NST o BPP con resultados anormales
treatment: Reposo en cama y control de actividad física
Hidratación oral o intravenosa materna según indicación
Suplementación de oxígeno materno si hay hipoxemia
Inducción de parto o cesárea si hay deterioro fetal
complications: Parto prematuro y bajo peso al nacer
Sufrimiento fetal agudo y muerte intrauterina
nursing_care: Evaluar movimientos fetales cada 12 h y registrar cambios
Monitorizar presión arterial, peso y edema materno
Controlar hidratación: ingesta ≥ 2 L/día y registrar salida urinaria
Realizar monitoreo fetal continuo (CTG) y reportar desaceleraciones
Preparar al paciente para posible inducción o cesárea
patient_teaching: Importancia de reportar disminución de movimientos fetales inmediatamente
Mantener hidratación adecuada y evitar actividades extenuantes
Asistir a todas las visitas prenatales y ecografías programadas
Señalar signos de alarma: sangrado, contracciones regulares, dolor abdominal intenso

care_plans.diagnosis: Riesgo de déficit de volumen de líquidos
outcomes: Volumen de líquido amniótico dentro de rango normal (AFI ≥ 8 cm)

interventions.action: Evaluar ingesta y salida de líquidos maternos cada 8 h
interventions.rationale: Permite detectar déficit hídrico temprano

interventions.action: Fomentar consumo de agua y jugos sin azúcar
interventions.rationale: Aumenta el volumen de líquido amniótico

interventions.action: Administrar hidratación intravenosa según indicación médica
interventions.rationale: Corrige déficit de volumen cuando la ingesta oral es insuficiente

interventions.action: Monitorear AFI mediante ecografía cada 1‑2 semanas
interventions.rationale: Evalúa respuesta al tratamiento y previene oligohidramnios severo

interventions.action: Educar a la paciente sobre signos de deshidratación (sed, orina oscura)
interventions.rationale: Facilita la detección precoz y la intervención oportuna

care_plans.diagnosis: Riesgo de perfusión tisular cerebral ineficaz
outcomes: Frecuencia cardíaca fetal dentro de rango (110‑160 lpm)
Movimientos fetales perceptibles al menos 10 veces en 2 h

interventions.action: Realizar monitoreo fetal continuo (CTG) y registrar patrones
interventions.rationale: Detecta signos de hipoxia y permite intervención temprana

interventions.action: Posicionar a la madre en decúbito lateral izquierdo
interventions.rationale: Mejora el flujo sanguíneo uteroplacentario

interventions.action: Administrar oxígeno suplementario a 2‑4 L/min por máscara facial si SpO₂ < 95 %
interventions.rationale: Aumenta la oxigenación materna y fetal

interventions.action: Evaluar y registrar movimientos fetales cada 12 h
interventions.rationale: Indicador clínico de perfusión cerebral fetal

interventions.action: Informar al médico ante desaceleraciones variables o pérdida de variabilidad
interventions.rationale: Facilita decisiones de manejo como inducción o cesárea

en.summary: Decreased ability of the placenta to transfer oxygen and nutrients to the fetus, causing growth restriction and possible oligohydramnios. Diagnosed via ultrasound and amniotic fluid index measurement.
key_points: Associated with fetal growth restriction and low amniotic fluid volume
Ultrasound diagnosis: AFI <5 cm or amniotic sac <500 mL
Management includes rest, maternal hydration, and fetal monitoring
Complications: preterm birth, fetal distress, and intrauterine death

pathophysiology: Placenta fails to achieve adequate perfusion due to insufficient vascular remodeling
Reduces oxygen and nutrient exchange between mother and fetus
Result: fetal hypoxia and reduced amniotic fluid volume
signs_symptoms: Uterine growth less than expected for gestational age
diagnostics: Obstetric ultrasound: AFI <5 cm or amniotic sac <500 mL
Umbilical artery Doppler: abnormal flow or increased resistance
Fetal biometry: percentile <10 for gestational age
Fetal well‑being tests: NST or BPP with abnormal results
treatment: Oral or intravenous maternal hydration as indicated
Maternal oxygen supplementation if hypoxemia present
Induction of labor or cesarean if fetal deterioration
complications: Preterm birth and low birth weight
Acute fetal distress and intrauterine death
nursing_care: Assess fetal movements every 12 h and document changes
Monitor maternal blood pressure, weight, and edema
Control hydration: intake ≥ 2 L/day and record urine output
Perform continuous fetal monitoring (CTG) and report decelerations
Prepare patient for possible induction or cesarean
patient_teaching: Importance of reporting decreased fetal movements immediately
Maintain adequate hydration and avoid strenuous activities
Attend all prenatal visits and scheduled ultrasounds
Identify warning signs: bleeding, regular contractions, severe abdominal pain

outcomes: Amniotic fluid volume within normal range (AFI ≥ 8 cm)

interventions.action: Assess maternal fluid intake and output every 8 h
interventions.rationale: Allows early detection of fluid deficit

interventions.action: Encourage consumption of water and unsweetened juices
interventions.rationale: Increases amniotic fluid volume

interventions.action: Administer intravenous hydration as ordered by physician
interventions.rationale: Corrects volume deficit when oral intake is insufficient

interventions.action: Monitor AFI via ultrasound every 1‑2 weeks
interventions.rationale: Evaluates treatment response and prevents severe oligohydramnios

interventions.action: Educate patient on signs of dehydration (thirst, dark urine)
interventions.rationale: Facilitates early detection and timely intervention

care_plans.diagnosis: Risk for ineffective cerebral tissue perfusion
outcomes: Fetal heart rate within range (110‑160 bpm)
Fetal movements perceptible at least 10 times in 2 h

interventions.action: Perform continuous fetal monitoring (CTG) and record patterns
interventions.rationale: Detects signs of hypoxia and allows early intervention

interventions.action: Position mother in left lateral decubitus
interventions.rationale: Improves uteroplacental blood flow

interventions.action: Administer supplemental oxygen at 2‑4 L/min via face mask if SpO₂ < 95 %
interventions.rationale: Increases maternal and fetal oxygenation

interventions.action: Assess and record fetal movements every 12 h
interventions.rationale: Clinical indicator of fetal cerebral perfusion

interventions.action: Notify physician of variable decelerations or loss of variability
interventions.rationale: Facilitates management decisions such as induction or cesarean

sections.pathophysiology.1.quote: A postterm pregnancy poses a threat for fetal growth restriction due to lack of perfusion of oxygen and nutrients associated with an aging placenta.

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: Risk factors for preeclampsia include nulliparity, extremes in maternal age, obesity, multiple gestation pregnancy, kidney disease, chronic hypertension , diabetes, and a personal or family history of preeclampsia.

sections.risk_factors.1.quote: Like preexisting diabetes, gestational diabetes can be associated with adverse maternal and fetal outcomes when blood glucose levels are not well controlled.

sections.risk_factors.2.quote: These conditions include multiple gestation, intrauterine fetal demise, and infection.

sections.risk_factors.3.quote: Gestational Trophoblastic Disease Patients below 20 years or above 40 years of age are at increased risk for abnormal growth of placental trophoblastic tissue during pregnancy.

sections.risk_factors.4.quote: Risk factors for preterm labor include previous preterm birth, infection, cervical abnormalities, chronic medical conditions, multiple gestation pregnancy, and certain lifestyle factors, such as substance use, smoking, poor diet, stress, and limited access to health care (Griggs et al., 2020).

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: Patients may experience decreased or absent fetal movement prior to diagnosis, which is one sign of impending fetal demise.

sections.signs_symptoms.2.quote: Signs of preeclampsia are high blood pressure, proteinuria, edema, headaches, vision changes, epigastric pain, and nausea or vomiting.

sections.signs_symptoms.3.quote: Placental abruption Vaginal bleeding, painful May cause maternal and fetal distress Signs of maternal and fetal hemorrhage Abdominal pain Cramping, uterine contractions Back pain

sections.diagnostics.0.quote: Diagnosis (via ultrasound) amniotic fluid index (AFI) < 5 cm amniotic fluid volume < 500 mL maximum fluid pocket < 2 cm

sections.treatment.0.quote: In cases of high risk for hemorrhage, patients may be placed on bed rest and pelvic rest until delivery.

sections.treatment.1.quote: Management includes close monitoring of the amniotic fluid volume as well as fetal status and hydration of the pregnant person using IV or oral fluids (Keilman & Shanks, 2024).

sections.treatment.3.quote: Continuous electronic fetal monitoring may be ordered to evaluate fetal heart rate and uterine contractions.

sections.treatment.4.quote: In cases of unstable pregnant person or fetal status, induction of labor or cesarean delivery may be performed.

sections.complications.1.quote: In cases of severe oligohydramnios, induction of labor is warranted.

sections.complications.2.quote: Complications related to hyperemesis gravidarum can negatively impact fetal outcomes and lead to low birth weight and preterm birth (Fejzo et al., 2019).

sections.nursing_care.4.quote: In cases of unstable pregnant person or fetal status, induction of labor or cesarean delivery may be performed.

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: Patients experiencing vaginal bleeding, abdominal cramping, decreased fetal movement, or signs of infection should immediately be evaluated by a health-care provider to assess maternal-fetal status.
